docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Personal App

docs.title: 1. Installation in Home Assistant
docs.text:
1. Add this addon repository to Home Assistant (https://github.com/aminedjeghri/ha-addons)
  2. Install the "Personal App" addon
  3. Configure your settings (see below)
  4. Start the addon
  5. Open the Web UI from the addon page

docs.title: 2. Installation in a local environment
docs.text:
This project is a monorepo containing two main packages:

  • frontend: A NiceGUI application.
  • backend: A FastAPI application that serves the AI models and business logic.

The project uses uv as a package manager and is configured as a workspace, so dependencies for both packages can be installed with a single command.

docs.title: 2.1. Local Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or macOS
  • UV & python (make install-uv, then make install-dev)
  • Create a .env file (take a look at the .env.example file)

docs.title: 2.2 ⚙️ Steps for Installation
docs.text: This project uses a Makefile to simplify the installation and execution process.

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text:
Once installed (either locally or via Docker), you can run the services.

  • Run Everything: make run starts the backend and the frontend together.

  • Run Services Individually:

    • Run Backend: make run-backend
    • Run Frontend: make run-frontend

You can then access:

  • Frontend (NiceGUI): http://localhost:8080 (or the configured port)
  • Backend (FastAPI): http://localhost:8000 (or the configured port). Docs http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: 3. Contributing
docs.text: Check CONTRIBUTING.md and the developer guide for more information.

docs.title: 4. Exposure & blocked URLs
docs.text:
LAN-only — do not publish. This add-on has no authentication anywhere, so every path is a must-never-be-public:

Path Why :8080/, /media/*, /static/*, /_nicegui/* Unauthenticated UI + websocket; the page exposes host metrics :8000/docs, :8000/openapi.json, :8000/api/* FastAPI docs and API are open, and CORS is * with credentials. Port 8000 is not published to the host, but any co-resident add-on container can reach it /robots.txt Disallow: (empty) — explicitly invites crawlers

SESSION_SECRET also falls back to change_this_secret when unset — set it if you ever expose this beyond a trusted network.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the contributors of this repository, who are responsible for enforcement, by opening an issue. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.0, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct.html.

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Follow Setup, then coordinate on an issue.
  2. Branch from main: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>.
  3. Update the relevant docs and run make check (Testing).
  4. Open a PR to main using a Conventional Commit title. PRs are squash-merged; the title determines the version.

CI runs the same checks for changes under addons/personal-app/; inspect its result after pushing. See Release for publication and recovery. Coding agents need explicit approval for commits, pushes and publishing. Follow the Code of Conduct; report security issues through SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/ha-addons/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Install the workspace and run the application locally.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Make, Bash, Git and uv on Ubuntu 22.04+ or macOS. uv provisions the Python version set by requires-python in pyproject.toml; run make install-uv if uv is missing. Docker is optional and only needed for make docker-build.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/ha-addons.git
cd ha-addons/addons/personal-app
make install-dev
cp .env.example .env

This installs backend, frontend and dev/docs tools and, in a Git checkout, the Git hooks. The hooks come from the repository-root .pre-commit-config.yaml and cover every add-on.

Before a pull request, run:

make check   # hooks, tests and the strict documentation build

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
make run
URL / command Use http://localhost:8080 Frontend http://localhost:8000/docs Backend API docs make run-backend / make run-frontend Start either side separately

docs.title: Home Assistant add-on image
docs.text: The Dockerfile is the add-on image: the Supervisor builds it and starts it through run.sh (bashio), so it cannot run standalone. make docker-build checks that it builds.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text: make deploy-doc-local

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text: Command Use make check The full local gate before a pull request make test-all Unit tests and the built-wheel smoke test make pre-commit Run the static hooks; FILES="path/a path/b" limits them to files make docs-build Strict documentation build make clean Remove caches and temporary files make help List all targets

docs.title: Optional environments
docs.text:
Command Use make install-prod Production dependencies only make install-tools Quality and docs tools without the application dependencies make install-release Packaging and release tools without the application dependencies make act Run GitHub Actions locally (make install-act first; needs Docker and .env)

For publication, see release credentials.

docs.title: Editor and agent rules
docs.text: Select .venv/bin/python; mark backend/src, frontend/src and tests as source/test roots. Agent rules live in AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md links to it for Claude Code.

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
A uv workspace with two packages that share one version and one git tag, packaged as a Home Assistant add-on.

pyproject.toml          workspace root: shared dev/docs tools, ruff, pytest, semantic-release, commitizen
backend/                package personal-app-backend (FastAPI)
  pyproject.toml        backend dependencies
  src/personal_app_backend/
    app.py              FastAPI application
    api/routes/metrics.py  host metrics route
    backend_settings.py settings (pydantic-settings, .env) and the loguru logger
frontend/               package personal-app-frontend (NiceGUI)
  src/personal_app_frontend/
    main.py             NiceGUI application
    components/metrics.py  metrics component
    frontend_settings.py
tests/unit/             backend, docs and release tooling tests
scripts/                commit parser, release artifact checks and workspace docs generators
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
docs/developer/         this guide
config.yaml build.json  Home Assistant add-on definition (version written by semantic-release)
Dockerfile run.sh       add-on image and its startup script
properdocs.yml          documentation site (MkDocs Material)
CHANGELOG.md            written by semantic-release, never by hand

The repository root (../../) holds what every add-on shares: .pre-commit-config.yaml, .github/ (workflows, Renovate, templates) and AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Where to add things
docs.text: Task Where Help a backend route backend/src/personal_app_backend/api/routes/ Add a backend route a setting backend_settings.py or frontend_settings.py Add a setting an add-on option config.yaml (options, schema) and run.sh Add an add-on option a dependency uv add --package <package> <pkg> Add a dependency a make target makefiles/<concern>.mk with a ## description —

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to the ApplicationSettings class in backend_settings.py (or frontend_settings.py). A secret is a SecretStr.
  2. Add it, with a safe example value, to .env.example.
  3. Read it through the module-level settings object.

docs.title: Add an add-on option
docs.text:
1. Add the option and its type to options and schema in config.yaml.
  2. Export it in run.sh with bashio::config, using the setting's environment variable name.
  3. Add the setting as above, so a local .env and the add-on behave the same.

docs.title: Add a backend route
docs.text:
1. Add the route in backend/src/personal_app_backend/api/routes/ (an APIRouter).
  2. Include the router in app.py.
  3. Add isolated API tests in tests/unit/backend/. The route appears in /docs automatically.

docs.title: Add a dependency
docs.text: uv add --package personal-app-backend <pkg> (or --package personal-app-frontend), then commit uv.lock. The Dockerfile installs from uv.lock with --frozen.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Use the make targets (make help): CI runs the same ones.
  • Docstrings on public functions and classes (Google style): they generate the API reference.
  • Settings come from backend_settings.py / frontend_settings.py (pydantic-settings, .env), never os.environ scattered in the code. Secrets are SecretStr.

  • Logging with the package's loguru logger, not print:

    from personal_app_backend.backend_settings import logger

logger.info("Loaded {} items", count)

  • Log, then raise; do not swallow exceptions:

    if not path.exists():
    logger.error(f"File not found: {path}. Current directory: {Path.cwd()}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(path)

    In an except block, logger.exception(...) logs the message and the stack trace. Not raising is fine only when a loop must go on after one failure.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Branch off main: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>.
  2. Run make check (4. Testing), then open a pull request to main. Its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  3. Pull requests are squash-merged. Pushes to main that touch this add-on are released by CI.

Never edit a version in pyproject.toml or config.yaml, or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does it.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Emoji Type Aliases Release 🐛 fix bugfix, hotfix patch ⚡️ perf patch ✨ feat feature minor 💥 feat! BREAKING CHANGE: footer major ♻️ 📝 🎨 🧪 🔧 👷 📦 refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none

A ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer makes any allowed type a breaking change (major release).

✨ feat(metrics): add disk usage
🐛 fix(backend): handle a missing sensor
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 endpoint

Scopes are optional. Common scopes: backend, frontend, addon, ci, deps. The commit message is checked on commit (commitizen) and the pull request title by ci.yml.

The repository holds other add-ons, and semantic-release reads every commit since the last personal-app-v* tag. Keep commits that touch several add-ons separate, or a change to another add-on can bump this one.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use environment variables or .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs on commit. For a line that intentionally references a secret placeholder (${{ secrets.X }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. File-level exclusions in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the setting in backend_settings.py or frontend_settings.py, .env.example, config.yaml and run.sh when it is an add-on option, and the workflow env: if CI needs it.

docs.title: Dependencies (Renovate)
docs.text: Renovate (.github/renovate.json5) opens pull requests with the renovate and dependencies labels for the whole repository. Review every one; a dependency dashboard issue lists the pending ones. uv.lock makes builds reproducible, and the add-on image installs from it.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text: Run the offline tests during development and the full gate before a pull request.

docs.title: Before a pull request
docs.text:
Complete setup, then run:

make check

make check runs pre-commit-status, pre-commit, test-all and docs-build (it first warns if the Git hooks are missing). test-all runs the unit tests, then builds both wheels and installs them in a throwaway environment to check that they import. There are no integration tests yet.

docs.title: Focused checks
docs.text:
Command Scope / requirement make check pre-commit-status, pre-commit, test-all and docs-build make test-local Unit tests only make test-all Every software suite, including the built-wheel smoke test make pre-commit Static hooks; FILES="path/a path/b" selects files make pre-commit-status Warn when the Git hooks are not installed make docs-build Strict docs build only make build-package Verify the backend/frontend wheel and sdist sets make docker-build Build the add-on image (requires Docker)

Tests use N=4 workers by default; use N=0 for serial diagnostics. Focused targets accept ARGS filters (make test-unit ARGS="-k release"); test-all rejects them. Unit tests and synthetic artifacts do not prove a container or a Home Assistant install works.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
Folder Tests tests/unit/backend/ Settings and isolated API checks tests/unit/docs/ API reference generation tests/unit/release/ Release tooling, with fake git, uv and gh

Parallel tests share no state. Release tooling tests use isolated command substitutes and never publish.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: ci.yml and release.yml run the reusable quality-and-tests.yml: pre-commit, then make test-all, only for changes under addons/personal-app/. See 5. Release.

docs.title: Static and documentation hooks
docs.text: Hooks check formatting and lint (Ruff), syntax and whitespace, secrets, Markdown and spelling, the lockfile and the strict docs build, workflow syntax (actionlint) and workflow security (zizmor). Commitizen runs only at the commit-msg stage. They live in the repository-root .pre-commit-config.yaml, scoped per add-on. make install-dev installs the Git hooks in a checkout (not in CI); make pre-commit only runs them.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish the backend and frontend packages to a GitHub Release (one wheel and one sdist each, never a package index), bump the add-on version and deploy the documentation to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Once, in the repository settings:

  • Actions → General → Workflow permissions: Read and write. The workflow declares permissions: {} and grants contents: read to the checks, contents: write to the release and docs jobs.
  • Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages.
  • Squash merging enabled, so the PR title decides the version (commit convention).

Locally, install the tooling and log in:

make install-dev
gh auth login

Credentials resolve from GH_TOKEN (environment or local .env), then the token saved by gh auth login, then a hidden terminal prompt. Never print credentials.

docs.title: What a release does
docs.text:
1. Validate the source: main or dev, clean tree, HEAD equal to the fetched origin tip, and in CI HEAD equal to the tested GITHUB_SHA.
  2. Version with semantic-release from Conventional Commits. Its build hook locks and builds every package before anything is committed, tagged or published.
  3. Commit, tag and push chore(release): personal-app-v<version> [skip ci]. The commit updates the three pyproject.toml versions, config.yaml (the version Home Assistant offers as an update), uv.lock and CHANGELOG.md.
  4. Upload the wheel and sdist of both packages to the GitHub Release.
  5. Deploy docs from the release tag, on a stable main release only.

Never edit a version, the changelog or a tag by hand. Tags look like personal-app-vX.Y.Z (personal-app-vX.Y.Z-rc.N on a dev branch); Python artifact names use X.Y.ZrcN.

docs.title: Automatic release (CI)
docs.text:
release.yml runs on a push to main (or dev) that touches addons/personal-app/**, and on manual dispatch. quality-checks is the gate; if it fails or is skipped, nothing is versioned or published. The release commit carries [skip ci], so its own push does not re-run the gate. Docs-only and chore commits bump no version.

A guard step skips the release when nothing under addons/personal-app/ changed since the last personal-app-v* tag, because semantic-release reads the commits of every add-on.

docs.title: Manual release (local)
docs.text:
make check
make release

It versions, builds and uploads the full wheel/sdist set, and asks you to type yes. It changes Git and GitHub; coding agents need explicit per-action approval. make release-status reports branch, tree, origin sync, tag and GitHub release without changing anything; run it when a release refuses.

Publish docs separately from the clean released tag with make deploy-doc-gh, which pushes gh-pages and needs separate authorization.

docs.title: The guard
docs.text:
The release refuses unless the branch is main or dev, the tree is clean (the whole repository, not just this folder) and HEAD equals origin/<branch>:

  • Dirty tree from hook fixes or a stale lock: commit it first, as chore(...).
  • Not in sync: git pull --rebase when behind, git push when ahead.

docs.title: Recover an interrupted release
docs.text:
Each stage is re-runnable and stops before publishing on a bad precondition: a failed build hook (uv lock && git add uv.lock && make build-package) stops everything before any commit, tag or upload, and make release-assets refuses when the tag is not at HEAD or a package has no wheel/sdist pair.

  • CI: rerun the failed job while its tested source still matches the release.
  • Same branch, locally: make release stops without uploading when nothing is left to publish.
  • From a clean checkout of the exact tag: make build-package, then make release-assets.
  • Newer commits exist: let their own workflow release them; never rebuild an older release from later source.

docs.title: Verify the release
docs.text:
• gh release view personal-app-vX.Y.Z --json assets,isDraft lists one wheel and one sdist per package, with isDraft: false.
  • config.yaml on main carries the new version, and Home Assistant offers the update.
  • Stable only: gh-pages has a new commit and the site shows the new version.

docs.title: Fix a bad release
docs.text: Fix forward: revert on main and let the next patch release carry the fix. Do not move, delete or re-create a published tag.

docs.title: lifespan(app) async
docs.text:
This function is called when the server starts.

Source code in backend/src/personal_app_backend/app.py 
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """This function is called when the server starts."""
    # Startup logic
    logger.info("Application startup: Initializing resources concurrently...")

    yield
    # Shutdown logic
    logger.info("Application shutdown.")

docs.title: setup_static_resources()
docs.text:
Set up static resources for the application.

Source code in frontend/src/personal_app_frontend/utils.py 
def setup_static_resources():
    """Set up static resources for the application."""
    # Get the project root directory (where the app is run from)
    project_root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
    resources_path = os.path.join(project_root, "resources")
    images_path = os.path.join(resources_path, "images")

    # Add static files directory for images
    app.add_static_files("/static", images_path)

    # Add media files directory for videos (using the same images directory since videos are there)
    app.add_media_files("/media", images_path)

docs.title: Test map
docs.text: Locate self-contained tests and run the existing validation commands.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
tests/unit/
├── backend/
│   ├── test_metrics.py             Metrics route: status and fields
│   └── test_settings.py            Settings defaults, environment overrides and logging
├── docs/test_doc_stubs.py          API references for packages and workspaces
└── release/
    ├── test_artifacts.py           Complete wheel/sdist sets, version and tag spelling
    ├── test_release_guards.py      Preconditions, failed commands and recovery
    ├── test_release_assets.py      Upload prerequisites and build ordering
    ├── conftest.py                 Temporary projects and command setup
    └── fixtures/release_command.py Fake Git, uv, GitHub and Make boundaries

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
1. Prepare the locked development tools with make install-dev.
  2. Run make test-all for every existing software test, using four pytest workers by default.
  3. Run make pre-commit for static hooks and strict docs, or make check for hooks and software tests.
  4. Use make docs-build independently when checking documentation.
  5. Run make build-package separately when artifact inputs change; synthetic test artifacts do not prove a real wheel installs or runs.

make test-unit ARGS="-k release" selects a focused diagnostic run. make test-all rejects filters. Release tests execute isolated command substitutes; they never publish or mutate this checkout.
